claims.text: Upper endoscopy in every patient to exclude cancer, with esophageal biopsies for eosinophilic esophagitis.
claims.quote: Patients with dysphagia should always have upper endoscopy, which is extremely important to exclude cancer ( 1 ). During endoscopy, esophageal biopsies should also be performed to evaluate for eosinophilic esophagitis .

claims.text: Barium swallow (with a solid bolus) if endoscopy cannot be done or finds no cause.
claims.quote: A barium swallow (with a solid bolus, usually a marshmallow or tablet) can be performed if the patient is unable to undergo an upper endoscopy or if upper endoscopy with biopsy does not identify a cause.

claims.text: Esophageal motility studies when both are normal.
claims.quote: If the barium swallow is negative and the upper endoscopy is normal, esophageal motility studies should be performed.
